To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of inter-document similarities can improve content-based Web search relevance, and that a probabilistic framework that decouples document query similarity and relevance estimation can be a powerful approach in noisy search settings.

(1) inter-document similarities can be used to improve relevance estimation, and (2) the use of query-independent document quality measures can improve the performance of relevance estimation approaches that rely on inter-document similarities, as well as on query-document similarities.
(1) document-query surface level similarities can be a misleading relevance signal, and (2) inter-document similarities in the initial retrieved list can help improve relevance estimation.

the problem of estimating relevance in the presence of misleading surface level similarities, using inter-document similarities in the list.
the problem of estimating the relevance of a document to a query, given a list of documents that are retrieved by a search engine, in an adversarial and noisy setting as the web.
the development of novel methods for ranking documents based on their similarity to each other, as well as to the query, and their quality, in the context of the Web.
